1. launcher_tests.ps1 nested host: the Windows PS host resolves a bare
   executable name through $env:PATHEXT. This box exports none and
   $env:PATHEXT reads '.CPL' inside the spawned host, so '& powershell
   -File ...' raised CommandNotFoundException while the same binary spawned
   fine from Python (CreateProcess ignores PATHEXT). Added Repair-PathExt +
   Resolve-NestedHost (PATH lookup, no hardcoded System32 path) +
   Assert-Host (SKIP, not FAIL).

2. test_launcher.py deleted the cross-process lock file at import. filelock
   4.x WindowsFileLock uses a LockFileEx byte-range lock the OS releases when
   the holder dies, so a leftover file cannot block acquisition, while the
   delete can drop the file out from under a LIVE holder. Removed it.

3. test_launch_watcher_for_grepai_ps1.py drove a suite targeting
   ###2.launch_watcher_for_grepai.ps1, which this checkout does not ship.
   SKIP when the target is absent.

4. test_watcher_allocator.py imported llm_fallback_proxy, whose file is
   ###2.llm_fallback_proxy.py - the '#' characters make it an invalid
   identifier, so the import aborted collection for the WHOLE repo. Now
   loaded by file location.

Pre-existing defects found while verifying:

5. 'Get-CimInstance Win32Process' (typo for Win32_Process) made T8's
   self-skip probe always false, so T8 never skipped even with a live
   launcher; it then fell into the interactive combined view and hung.
6. T10b/T10d assumed .grepai/index.gob, absent on qdrant-backed installs.
7. $watchersWorkspaceRoot was unset in the harness (the extracted health
   block is workspace-scoped); T11/T12 pointed $scriptDir instead.
8. T23 killed the tailer on a fixed 3s deadline, before the resume marker
   was flushed.

4719d044b2832784516a87c4116e524108f28e92uni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.comuni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.com17896914862026-09-18T12:31:26+12:003f5c8fcfb5f940c3204cc997fc9dabd82bbbc4f3fix(launcher): prune degraded grepai worktrees (mcpw-759)The Layer 1 prune guard was 'if ($wtHead -and $wtHead -eq $mainHead)'. A
half-constructed worktree makes 'git -C <wt> rev-parse HEAD' print nothing and
exit 128, so $wtHead was empty, the guard was FALSE, and the degraded worktree
was skipped in silence on every run. 'git worktree remove --force' refuses such
a path too ('fatal: validation failed, cannot remove working tree'), so nothing
ever cleaned it up and grepai re-used the dead directory and failed to index.

Measured on a throwaway repo (temp/mcpw759) with the real git, .git gitfile
deleted or truncated:
  rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree  -> (no output)              exit 128
  rev-parse HEAD                   -> (no output)              exit 128
  status --porcelain               -> fatal: not a git repo    exit 128
  worktree remove <wt> --force     -> fatal: validation failed exit 128
  worktree list --porcelain        -> STILL LISTS THE PATH

Changes:
- Test-GitWorktreeUsable: new. Keys on 'rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' plus a
  toplevel identity check. Identity is required because a degraded directory
  NESTED inside another repository makes --is-inside-work-tree answer 'true'
  for the OUTER repo (measured); without it a nested dead path reads healthy.
- Invoke-GrepaiWorktreePrune: new (was inline). Removes a candidate git lists
  but cannot open, then falls back to deleting the directory only after git's
  own 'worktree remove --force' refuses. Rejects blank paths: PS 5.1 DROPS a
  null operand, turning 'git -C "$wt" rev-parse HEAD' into 'git -C rev-parse
  HEAD' -> "fatal: cannot change to 'rev-parse'", which aborts the whole block
  under ErrorActionPreference=Stop. That is the T6/T7 warning; see new bead
  mcpw-9lf for the call sites still unguarded.
- Never removes: the main worktree, the workspace root, or any parent of it.
  Only two path sources are considered - git's own 'worktree list' output and
  the launcher's own <repo>\<workspaceKey>\worktree scaffolding path.
- Dirty guard kept for healthy worktrees. It cannot apply to a degraded one:
  there is no index or HEAD there, and 'status' cannot answer at all.
- Ordering: Layer 1 (prune) now runs BEFORE Layer 2 (validate). Layer 2 keeps
  its purpose - it still drops a stale .grepai/index.gob in surviving
  worktrees - but no longer validates a path Layer 1 is about to delete.
- Candidates deduped on the normalized path: 'worktree list' prints forward
  slashes while Join-Path yields backslashes, so each path was walked twice.

Tests: tests/launcher_worktree_prune_corrupt.tests.ps1 (new, Pester 3.4.0, AST
extraction of the production functions, real git in a throwaway repo, cleanup
in a finally block). 7 passed, 0 failed.
tests/test_launcher_worktree_quoting.py: re-pin the --show-toplevel assertion
from $scriptDir to $watchersWorkspaceRoot - 026765e removed the old string and
left this gate red at HEAD.

Every touched file parse-checked: 0 errors.

Commit 1f14b57 removed the npm shim at the source (absolute node.exe
plus memtrace.js), but the two heal spawn sites still launched the child
without -PassThru, so a child that failed the heal verdict was never tracked
and never reaped.

- Capture -PassThru at both spawn sites; track the child in a runspace-local
  hashtable ($memtraceHealChild.Proc).
- Stop-MemtraceHealChild tree-kills the tracked child (Stop-WatcherTree from
  Modules/watcher_teardown.ps1, dot-sourced from a path derived from the
  helpers module). Called when the 45s verdict window expires with the ports
  still down, and on permanent store-scope refusal. The handle is cleared when
  the heal succeeds, so the healthy daemon is never reaped.
- The tracked-child set is deliberately runspace-local: the ThreadJob cannot
  reach the launcher global WatcherChildren set, and the launcher rewrites
  teardown-state.json AFTER the job starts, so appending PIDs there would race
  and be lost.
- Stop-OrphanedMemtraceHosts / Get-OrphanedMemtraceHostPids sweep leftover shim
  hosts from earlier builds at launcher start. Narrow and PID-scoped: only a
  Windows PowerShell or pwsh host whose command line names the memtrace shim
  AND whose parent is gone, so live launchers and the memtrace daemon never
  match.
- tests/launcher_memtrace_heal.tests.ps1 (Pester 3.4.0, real processes, no
  mocks): 5 passed, 0 failed.

so a repo releases its OWN mutex instead of another repo's.
